title: Centrality of normal subgroups from their neutral components
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group, and let $N\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed normal subgroup scheme. Group schemes and closed normal subgroups are as in [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Reductive means smooth, connected, affine of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup, as in [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. Let $N^0$ be the connected component of its identity with the open-subscheme structure, as in [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component]; in particular it is not replaced by its reduction. Then $N^0$ is a closed normal subgroup scheme of $G$, and $N$ is central in $G$ if and only if $N^0$ is central in $G$. Here central means that for every commutative $k$-algebra $B$, every point of the subgroup over $B$ commutes with every point of $G$ after every commutative $B$-algebra extension. Neither $N$ nor $N^0$ is assumed smooth, reduced or connected beyond the defining connectedness of $N^0$.

proof.text: Write $C=N^0$. Since $G$ is affine of finite type, write $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finitely generated over $k$. The affine description of a closed immersion gives $N=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, so $N$ is also affine of finite type. Apply lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component to $N$: $C$ is a clopen subgroup scheme with its open structure and is geometrically irreducible. It is closed in $G$: on an affine chart, composing the two closed immersions composes two surjective ring maps. Apply the same component lemma to $G$. Connectedness of $G$ gives $G=G^0$, so $G$ too is geometrically irreducible. None of these assertions replaces $C$ by its reduction.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component; finite-type specialization. Affine closed-immersion description: Tag 01QO.

proof.text: Normality of $N$ makes conjugation a morphism $a:G\times_k C\to N$, $(g,c)\mapsto gcg^{-1}$. The source is irreducible by lem-sc-irreducible-product-over-field, hence connected. Its image is connected and contains the identity, so it lies in the identity component $|C|$ of $|N|$. By lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme, $a$ factors through the actual open subscheme $C$. Consequently for every $k$-algebra $B$, conjugation by every $g\in G(B)$ preserves $C(B)$; applying this also to $g^{-1}$ gives equality. Thus $C$ is normal in $G$, as a subgroup scheme, with no restriction on nilpotents in $B$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, connected-image argument applied to conjugation; product irreducibility: varieties.tex, Tag 038F.

proof.text: Assume now that $C$ is central in $G$. Fix any $n\in N(k)$, viewed as a constant point over every $k$-algebra. Normality defines a morphism $b_n:G\to N$ by $b_n(g)=gng^{-1}n^{-1}$. Its image is connected because $G$ is connected, and $b_n(e)=e$, so it lies in $|C|$. Factor it uniquely through the open subscheme to get $b_n:G\to C$. For every $B$ and $x,y\in G(B)$, the group identity gives $b_n(xy)=x b_n(y)x^{-1}b_n(x)$. Since $b_n(y)\in C(B)$ is central, this is $b_n(y)b_n(x)=b_n(x)b_n(y)$. Therefore $b_n$ is a group-scheme homomorphism to the commutative group scheme $C$. The calculation holds over every algebra, rather than just on rational points.

source.place: Section 12(j), derived groups, and Proposition 12.46; agent-written commutator calculation implementing Conrad Theorem 3.3.4, printed p.100.

proof.text: By lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient, the radical $R=R(G)$ is a central torus and the represented fppf quotient $G/R$ is semisimple. All hypotheses of lem-sfb-central-torus-semisimple-derived-product therefore hold. Put $D=G^{\mathrm{der}}$; that node supplies the faithfully flat multiplication $m:R\times_kD\to G$ and characterizes $D$ as the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator of $G$ factors. Since $b_n$ is a homomorphism with commutative target, it sends every commutator to $e$. Its kernel $K\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup by lem-sc-kernel-subgroup; the commutator morphism factors through $K$, so $D\subseteq K$ by that characterization. Also $b_n|_R=e$, since $R$ is central in $G$ and hence commutes with $n$. It follows that $b_n\circ m=e$ as morphisms.

source.place: Corollary 17.62(b),(d), pp.372--373; Proposition 12.46(b), pp.245--246; Proposition 21.60 proof, p.442.

proof.text: All schemes in the last equality are affine: $C$ is closed in the affine $N$, and $R,D,G$ are affine. On coordinate rings, $m^*:k[G]\to k[R\times_kD]$ is faithfully flat. It is injective by lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction, with the ideal zero. The equality $b_n\circ m=e$ says that the two maps $k[C]\rightrightarrows k[G]$ induced by $b_n$ and the constant identity morphism become equal after this injective map. They are equal already, so $b_n=e$. Thus this fixed $n\in N(k)$ commutes with every point of $G$ over every $k$-algebra, including after any further algebra extension.

Apply lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates to the finite-type group scheme $N$. Its finitely many clopen components are $n_j C$, with $n_j\in N(k)$, and translation identifies each with $C$ as schemes. Step 5 applies to every $n_j$. On $G\times_k(n_j C)$ write a point of the second factor as $n_jc$ using this translation isomorphism. For every $B$, both $n_j$ and $c\in C(B)$ commute with every $g\in G(B)$, so $g(n_jc)g^{-1}(n_jc)^{-1}=e$. Hence the commutator morphism $G\times_kN\to G$ is the identity constant on each member of this open cover and therefore on all of $G\times_kN$. This proves centrality of $N$ over every algebra and every further extension, even when a test scheme meets several components. Conversely if $N$ is central, its subgroup $C$ is central by restricting the same identity. Together with step 2 this proves both claims.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q04-c77b36522 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 12 cited statements; the delivery has no new nodes. Step 1: the identity-component lemma gives N^0 clopen and geometrically irreducible with its open (unreduced) structure, and closed in G. Step 2: G×N^0 is irreducible (product lemma); its conjugation image lies in the open N^0, so the factorization is legitimate (open target) and gives functorial normality. Step 3: I checked by expansion that b_n(xy)=x b_n(y) x^-1 b_n(x), so b_n is a homomorphism to the commutative central N^0. Step 4: radical-quotient gives R central torus and G/R semisimple, which are the hypotheses of central-torus-derived-product; D ⊆ ker b_n via lem-sc-kernel-subgroup, and b_n|_R=e (Milne iAG 12.46(b) p.245 and 17.62(b),(d) p.373 agree). Step 5: m^* is faithfully flat, hence injective (I=0), so b_n=e as morphisms. Step 6: the translates lemma gives an open cover by n_jN^0 with n_j rational, and equality is local. Small cases (μ_m in GL_n in char p, torus, N=1 or G) hold; the Heisenberg and finite-constant cases show the reductive and connected hypotheses are needed. No duplicate in the DAG (rg -L) and no cycle. I accept the 3 tool_uses (product irreducibility, kernel subgroup, faithfully flat injectivity) as general tools.
